part.pawnChain.title: Pawn chain and pawn break
part.pawnChain.summary: Attack the chain at its base with a pawn move and use the square the wedge controls; the position decides when to break.
ex.pc.7fycj: Play Black and find the best move.
ex.pc.7fycj.hint: Count who defends the f2 pawn and who can attack it.
ex.pc.7fycj.solution: 14...Qxf2#! The queen goes down the f-file, free of pawns, and captures the f2 pawn with mate: the f8 rook defends it. Before thinking about attacking the b4–c5 chain, check for mate.
ex.pc.A6wUE: Play White and find the best move.
ex.pc.A6wUE.hint: See which squares the black king still has and which move takes them away.
ex.pc.A6wUE.solution: 21.fxe5#! The pawn captures the e5 pawn, the base of the black chain, with checkmate: the h5 rook covers the fifth rank, the g1 rook the g-file, and the c4 bishop the e6 and f7 squares.
ex.pc.qrY7n: Play White and find the best move.
ex.pc.qrY7n.hint: Look for a square next to the black king that no black pawn can contest.
ex.pc.qrY7n.solution: 17.Qf6#! The queen goes to f6, the square the e5 wedge controls, with checkmate.
ex.pc.ZRfNw: Play Black and find the best move.
ex.pc.ZRfNw.hint: Count the black pieces aimed at the white king.
ex.pc.ZRfNw.solution: 31...gxf2#! The pawn captures the f2 pawn with check, and the g8 rook also gives check along the open g-file: the king has no square. Mate comes before any plan against the d4–e3 chain.
ex.pc.pkqzg: Play Black and find the best move.
ex.pc.pkqzg.hint: Look for a move that attacks two white pieces at once.
ex.pc.pkqzg.solution: 13...cxd4! The pawn captures the d4 pawn, the base of the d4–e5 chain, attacks the e3 queen and opens the e7 bishop's diagonal to a3. After 14.Nxd4, 14...Bxa3 captures the bishop.
ex.pc.Y3faf: Play White and find the best move.
ex.pc.Y3faf.hint: Think about what the e-file and the black king on e8 have in common.
ex.pc.Y3faf.solution: 20.e6! The wedge advances as a break: it attacks the d7 queen and opens the e-file. After 20...Qxe6, 21.Re5 pins the queen to the e8 king, with the rook defended by the d4 pawn, and White wins the queen.
ex.pc.Byqxd: Play Black and find the best move.
ex.pc.Byqxd.hint: Look for a move with check that leaves a white piece with no way out.
ex.pc.Byqxd.solution: 15...fxe4+! The pawn captures the e4 pawn, the base of the e4–d5 chain, and opens the f-file for the f8 rook, with check. After 16.Bf3, 16...Qxe1+ 17.Kxe1 exf3, and Black wins the piece back with a decisive advantage.
ex.pc.HGyly: Play White and find the best move.
ex.pc.HGyly.hint: Look for the black piece that only the queen defends and a move that pulls the queen away from it while gaining time.
ex.pc.HGyly.solution: 24.d5+! The isolated pawn advances, opens the queen's diagonal to g7 with check and attacks the c6 pawn, the base of the black chain. After 24...Qf6, 25.Qxa5 captures the rook.
ex.pc.cYgGT: Play White and find the best move.
ex.pc.cYgGT.hint: The black king on b6 is close to your queenside pawns.
ex.pc.cYgGT.solution: 38.c5+! The pawn gives check and attacks the d6 pawn, in the middle of the c7–d6–e5 chain. After 38...Kb7, 39.cxd6 opens the chain: the d6 pawn attacks the base on c7, which the f7 queen and the c2 rook also attack, and it falls.
part.passedPawn.title: Majority and passed pawn
part.passedPawn.summary: With more pawns on one wing, create a passed pawn and push it with the support of the pieces; blocked by a piece, it may become a target.
ex.pp.a4Pik: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.pp.a4Pik.hint: Your e7-pawn is passed and one step from promotion. Look at what it can capture.
ex.pp.a4Pik.solution: 29.exf8=Q#! The pawn captures the f8-queen and promotes with mate: the new queen, defended by the d8-queen, leaves the king no square. 29.exf8=R# is also mate; 29.Qxf8+? draws (29...Rxf8), and 29.Qd5+? loses (29...Qf7).
ex.pp.l7KBi: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.pp.l7KBi.hint: Your f7-pawn is passed and on the seventh rank. Look at the black king's squares.
ex.pp.l7KBi.solution: 24.f8=Q#! The pawn promotes with check, and the new queen watches g7 and g8: the black king has no square. 24.Rxd4? captures the queen, but after 24...Kg7 the advantage is small.
ex.pp.mLQkx: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.pp.mLQkx.hint: You have the queenside majority: three pawns against two. Also look at the d2-knight.
ex.pp.mLQkx.solution: 30...c3! The pawn slips past the b3-pawn, becomes passed and attacks the d2-knight. After 31.Ne4, 31...c2 threatens to promote on c1, a square the knight cannot reach. 30...cxb3? 31.Nxb3, 30...Nb6? and 30...Nb2? leave White better.
ex.pp.6FnQW: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.pp.6FnQW.hint: White's f5-pawn is passed, but your king blocks it. Also look at the two rooks on the e-file.
ex.pp.6FnQW.solution: 38...Rxf5+! The rook captures the blocked passed pawn with check and opens the e-file for the e6-rook. After 39.Kg4, 39...Rxe1 captures the rook. 38...Rxe1? 39.fxe6 and 38...Kxf5? 39.Rxe5 leave White better.
ex.pp.ePzmb: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.pp.ePzmb.hint: Your c3- and d2-pawns are passed and side by side. Look at the squares the e3-knight watches.
ex.pp.ePzmb.solution: 43...Rxe3+! The rook gives itself up to deflect the knight, which watched d1 and c2. After 44.Kxe3, 44...d1=Q promotes. 43...c2? 44.Kxd2, 43...Rd8? 44.Nd1 and 43...Rc8? 44.Kd1 leave White better.
ex.pp.wzBvs: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.pp.wzBvs.hint: Your d7-pawn is one step from promotion, but the a8-rook watches d8. Look at the a6-knight.
ex.pp.wzBvs.solution: 27.Rxa6! The rook captures the knight to deflect the a8-rook. After 27...Rxa6, 28.d8=Q+ promotes with check; 28.Rxa6?? allows 28...Rc1#. 27.d8=Q+? 27...Rxd8 loses the pawn, and 27.h3? or 27.g3? let 27...Rd8 stop it.
ex.pp.t5c4H: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.pp.t5c4H.hint: Your e3-pawn is passed and advanced. Look at what it attacks and what the c2-queen blocks.
ex.pp.t5c4H.solution: 39...exf2+! The pawn captures with check and attacks the e1-knight. After 40.Qxf2, the queen leaves the diagonal between f5 and b1, and 40...Qxb1 captures the rook; 40...Qxf2+? 41.Kxf2 trades queens, and Black is a piece down. 39...Qxc2? 40.Nxc2 leaves White better.
ex.pp.eIwhv: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.pp.eIwhv.hint: Your b7-pawn is one step from promotion, but the b3-rook watches it along the b-file. Look at the black king.
ex.pp.eIwhv.solution: 57.Rc3! The rook pins the b3-rook to the a3-king: it can only capture on c3 and leaves the b-file. After 57...Rxc3, 58.b8=Q promotes. 57.Kd6?, 57.Kd5? and 57.Rxh7? draw.
